headline: Inferring single-cell and spatial expression from histology and multi-omics models
label: Spatial Omics Representation Learning
summary: Histology-driven expression prediction is shifting toward program-level targets, while generative omics integration scales to 100 million cells.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learning mappings between histology or single-cell modalities and molecular readouts, using generative and representation models to predict, enhance, or integrate expression. VOICE combines contrastive alignment, direct regression and retrieval to predict in-situ single-cell expression from H&E, while program-space diffusion predicts cNMF-derived transcriptional programs rather than individual genes. VISTA applies histology-based spatial inference to prognostic and therapy-response analyses in cancer cohorts. MBTA links modality-specific latent spaces via flow matching, and PIANO integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics at scale to over 100 million cells. What is new is the shift of prediction targets from genes to programs and generative integration at this scale; trajectory inference, deconvolution and segmentation items address adjacent problems.
